title: Quantification of cell death and proliferation of ovarian cancer organoids through 3D imaging
author: Skorda, Lauridsen, et al.

steps.title: Prepare BME‑2 matrix
steps.instruction: Thaw a fresh 5 mL aliquot of BME‑2 on ice (4 °C) for 12–18 h, keep all tools on ice, pre‑cool pipette tips with cold PBS, adjust to 7.5 mg/mL protein by diluting with cold PBS, calculate the exact volume needed plus 10 % extra, mix gently without bubbles, and keep the diluted BME‑2 on ice (do not refreeze).

steps.title: Prepare staining reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions fresh as follows:

substeps.instruction: Live/Dead solution: add 4 µL Hoechst 33342 and 4 µL propidium iodide to 1 mL cold PBS; prepare fresh each use.
Fixation buffer (4 % FA): mix 4.3 mL 37 % PFA with 5.7 mL PBS.
Quenching buffer (0.2 M glycine): dissolve 1.5 g glycine in 100 mL PBS; store ≤ 1 month at 4 °C.
Permeabilization buffer (0.5 % Triton X‑100): add 500 µL Triton X‑100 to 100 mL PBS; store ≤ 1 month at 4 °C.
Washing buffer (3 % BSA): dissolve 3 g BSA in 100 mL PBS; store ≤ 1 month at 4 °C.
Blocking buffer: combine 3 µg BSA, 0.1 % Triton X‑100, 0.05 % Tween‑20 in PBS to a final volume of 100 mL; store ≤ 1 month at 4 °C.

steps.title: Cytotoxicity image analysis (Staining 1)
steps.instruction: Using MetaXpress on the 384‑well plate images, identify total and dead nuclei and export counts.

substeps.instruction: In the custom module workflow select ‘Find Round Objects’ on the Hoechst (DAPI) channel to detect all nuclei (total cells).
Select ‘Find Round Objects’ on the Texas Red (PI) channel to detect PI‑positive nuclei (dead cells).
Use ‘Keep marked objects’ to intersect PI‑positive nuclei with Hoechst nuclei, defining dead cells.
Set the mask of objects to measure as all DAPI nuclei; set ‘Features within each object’ to the dead‑cell mask.
Choose output ‘Count of objects’.
Export the measurements as summed values per site.

steps.title: Day 1 immunofluorescent staining (Staining 2)
steps.instruction: Perform fixation, quenching, permeabilization, blocking and primary antibody incubation on organoids in 96‑well plates (all incubations with gentle shaking at 15–25 °C unless noted).

substeps.instruction: Remove 100 µL media from each well, leaving 100 µL covering the organoids.
Add 35 µL fixation buffer to achieve a final 4 % FA concentration; incubate 15 min.
Wash 3 × with 100 µL PBS for 5 min each to remove FA.
Pause point (optional): cover plate with parafilm and store at 4 °C for up to 2 months.
Add 100 µL quenching buffer; incubate 15 min.
Wash 3 × with 100 µL washing buffer for 10 min each.
Add 100 µL permeabilization buffer; incubate 15 min.
Wash 3 × with 100 µL washing buffer for 10 min each.
Add 100 µL blocking buffer; incubate 1–2 h.
Add 70 µL primary antibody mix (diluted in blocking buffer): Ki67 (mouse) 1:150 and E‑cadherin (rat) 1:250; incubate 16–24 h at 4 °C with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Day 2 immunofluorescent staining (Staining 2)
steps.instruction: Apply secondary antibodies, nuclear stain, and final PBS while preserving the BME‑2 matrix.

substeps.instruction: Wash 3 × with 100 µL blocking buffer for 10 min each to remove excess primary antibody.
Add 70 µL secondary antibody mix (diluted in blocking buffer): Donkey anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 594 and Goat anti‑rat Alexa Fluor 488; incubate 2 h at 15–25 °C with gentle shaking.
Wash 3 × with 100 µL blocking buffer for 10 min each.
Wash once with 100 µL PBS for 5 min.
Add 70 µL Hoechst‑33258 (1:1000 in PBS); incubate 30 min.
Wash 3 × with 100 µL PBS for 10 min each.
Add 200 µL PBS for imaging; ensure at least 200 µL remains per well and leave 10–15 µL covering the BME‑2‑embedded organoids (do not let the tip touch the bottom).
Critical pause point (optional): cover plate with parafilm and foil, store at 4 °C for up to 3 months.

steps.title: Ki67 image analysis (Staining 2)
steps.instruction: Analyze Ki67‑stained images in MetaXpress to quantify proliferating nuclei.

substeps.instruction: In the custom module workflow select ‘Cell Scoring Objects’ on DAPI and FITC channels to detect nuclei with surrounding cytoplasmic marker.
Apply 3D ‘Connect by touching’ to create a 3D organoid mask across z‑stacks.
Use 3D ‘Connect by best match’ on the nuclei mask to define 3D nuclei.
Filter nuclei by Texas Red intensity to isolate Ki67‑positive nuclei (set appropriate threshold).
Apply 3D ‘Connect by best match’ to the Ki67‑positive nuclei to generate a 3D Ki67 mask.
In the measurement pane set the mask of objects to measure as the 3D organoid mask; add two features: total 3D nuclei (DAPI) and 3D Ki67‑positive nuclei (Texas Red).
Set output to ‘Count of objects’ and export measurements as mean values per site.
